summary: Illinois-born Harry Hoxsey sold an arsenic paste and herbal tonics as a cancer cure from the 1920s to 1960, ran a huge Dallas clinic, and fought the AMA and FDA in court while desperate patients died.

evidence.note: Hoxsey's birth in Auburn, Illinois in 1901
Taylorville institute operating and killing patients by 1924
moves operation to Dallas in 1936, his base for decades
uses a senator's hearing and patient testimony as marketing
long segment on alliance with antisemitic preacher Gerald Winrod
American Rally: anti-fluoride, anti-polio-vaccine allies backing Hoxsey
FDA's first public denunciation of a cancer cure and post office posters
permanent injunction ends legal US practice from 1960
nurse opens Tijuana clinic in 1963, seeding Baja cancer clinic industry
prostate cancer in 1967, later death in seclusion
teen with bone cancer dies after skipping amputation for Hoxsey tonics
escharotic paste destroys facial tissue and bone, fatal hemorrhage

notes: Death year is garbled in the transcript; 1974 from general knowledge. Tijuana clinic (1963 on), Laetrile clinics and modern Hoxsey sellers treated as legacy via reaches_present rather than extending covered_span. US-TX chosen as Dallas was his base 1936-1960, though Illinois features early. child-death rests on two short but specific cases.
